GridKit set up

1. MacPorts set up: 
Downloading the MacPorts for would allow to manage, install different compilors and development tools from the command line.
 Downaload and insatll MacPorts from macports.org.
 To update the version and get newest LLVM 18 package run:
    sudo port selfupdate
 
 To install the tools needed run:
sudo port install cmake 
// generates build instructions and tells the compiler what files to compile and how to link them together.

sudo port install ninja 
// fast build tool that actually executes the compilation steps generated by CMake.

sudo port install git
 // to download and manage source code repositories from sites like GitHub.

sudo port install python314
sudo port select --set python python314
sudo port select --set python3 python314

note: to switch shells in the mac: for z run ~/.zprofile and for bash ~/.bash_profile 

Dependencies:
Build order matters — each depends on the previous:
1. MacPorts tools (cmake, ninja, git, python314)
2. LLVM 18 + Clang 18 (compiler for everything below)
3. SuiteSparse/KLU (math library for SUNDIALS)
4. SUNDIALS (ODE/DAE solver, requires KLU)
5. Enzyme AD (autodiff plugin, requires LLVM 18)
6. GridKit (requires SUNDIALS + Enzyme)

Librararies:
SuiteSparse (responsible for KLU) // SuiteSparse_KLU for sparse linear solvers in SUNDIALS.

 
2. LLVM-18.
LLVM 18
│
├── Clang 18      ← C/C++ compiler
├── LLVM libraries
├── Optimizers

- llvm-18 and clang-18 are the specific LLVM/Clang version required by GridKit and Enzyme. Apple's built-in clang is a modified version that lags behind upstream LLVM.
~ change to the clang compilor. 
sudo port install llvm-18
sudo port install clang-18
sudo port select --set clang mp-clang-18

CMake = tells the compiler what files to compile and how to put everything together.

3. Sundails 
start working on "sundails" which is a first layer for the GridKit
// every directory will need to have "insall" and "build"

sundials/
├── sundials/     ← source
├── build/        ← compiler output
└── install/      ← finished installation (builded thought build directory and compiles to the install afterwards)

1. Clone Sundails:  
cd ~/Desktop/ORNLproject/src/sundials
git clone https://github.com/LLNL/sundials.git //to clone

Initial Sundails was given the arrow as we need to:
SUNDIALS_ENABLE_KLU = ON 
if not: CMake silently accepted the unknown variable, logged it as UNINITIALIZED, and built SUNDIALS without KLU support.

If the issue occured, check the build directory in sundails:
    cat ~/Desktop/ORNLproject/src/sundials/build/CMakeCache.txt | grep -i klu
    sudo port install SuiteSparse_KLU

Using sundails:
Sundauls uses the Cmake while the default was changed to 

cmake ~/Desktop/ORNLproject/src/sundials/sundials \
  -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=~/Desktop/ORNLproject/src/sundials/install \
  -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=/opt/local/libexec/llvm-18/bin/clang \
  -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=/opt/local/libexec/llvm-18/bin/clang++ \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo \
  -DSUNDIALS_ENABLE_KLU=ON \
  -DKLU_INCLUDE_DIR=/opt/local/include \
  -DKLU_LIBRARY_DIR=/opt/local/lib
make -j$(sysctl -n hw.logicalcpu) && make install

Stale CMakeCache.txt preserves old broken values even when you pass correct flags.
cd ~/Desktop/ORNLproject/src/sundials/build
rm -rf *

2. Enzyme AD: Enzyme is an automatic differentiation (AD) plugin for LLVM.
Enzyme automatically generates code that computes derivatives (gradients, sensitivities, Jacobians, etc.).

cd ~/Desktop/ORNLproject/src/enzymeAD
git clone https://github.com/EnzymeAD/Enzyme

Repo root: Enzyme/  — contains CMakeLists.txt for the full monorepo
Build target: Enzyme/enzyme/  — the actual Enzyme plugin source with its own CMakeLists.txt

⚠ If you run cmake from the repo root (Enzyme/) pointing at ../llvm, CMake errors saying the llvm source directory does not exist. Always cd into enzyme/ first.

Build Enzyme:
cd ~/Desktop/ORNLproject/src/enzymeAD/Enzyme/enzyme

mkdir build && cd build
cmake .. \
  -G Ninja \
  -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=/opt/local/libexec/llvm-18/bin/clang \
  -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=/opt/local/libexec/llvm-18/bin/clang++ \
  -DLLVM_DIR=/opt/local/libexec/llvm-18/lib/cmake/llvm \
  -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS="-stdlib=libc++" \ 
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=~/Desktop/ORNLproject/src/enzymeAD/install
ninja 
ninja install
// Ninja builds the intructions generated by CMake and finds files that needs compling, then calls clang 18 on those files and links everything together into the Enzyme library.

Ninja Vs Make:
Ninja is faster, better at parallel builds. 

To varify the Installment: 
find ~/Desktop/ORNLproject/src/enzymeAD/install -name '*Enzyme-18.dylib'

The outcome suppose to be; 
✓  ./lib/LLVMEnzyme-18.dylib
✓  ./lib/LLDEnzyme-18.dylib
✓  ./lib/ClangEnzyme-18.dylib


3. GridKit: providing a modeling framework for power systems simulations and analysis that can support multiple advanced analysys methods, such as dynamic constrained optimization and partitioned numerical integrators for systems of differential and algebraic equations.
Step 1: Clone GridKit + Submodules
cd ~/Desktop/ORNLproject/src/ornl_gridkit
git clone https://github.com/ORNL/GridKit.git
cd GridKit
git submodule update --init third-party/

GridKit's build directory must be a sibling of the source directory, not inside it:

Correct:  ornl_gridkit/build/  (sibling of GridKit/)
Wrong:    ornl_gridkit/GridKit/build/  (inside source)

cd ~/Desktop/ORNLproject/src/ornl_gridkit
mkdir build && cd build


CMake configuration:
cmake ../GridKit \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo \
  -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=/opt/local/libexec/llvm-18/bin/clang \
  -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=/opt/local/libexec/llvm-18/bin/clang++ \
  -DSUNDIALS_DIR=~/Desktop/ORNLproject/src/sundials/install \
  -DEnzyme_DIR=~/Desktop/ORNLproject/src/enzymeAD/install/lib/cmake/Enzyme \
  -DENZYME_LLVM_PLUGIN_LIBRARY= ~/Desktop/ORNLproject/src/enzymeAD/install/lib/LLVMEnzyme-18.dylib \
  -DENZYME_CLANG_PLUGIN_LIBRARY= ~/Desktop/ORNLproject/src/enzymeAD/install/lib/ClangEnzyme-18.dylib \
  -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=~/Desktop/ORNLproject/src/ornl_gridkit/install \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_SYSROOT="$(xcrun --sdk macosx --show-sdk-path)" \
  -DCMAKE_EXE_LINKER_FLAGS="-Wl,-rpath,/opt/local/lib" \
  -DCMAKE_SHARED_LINKER_FLAGS="-Wl,-rpath,/opt/local/lib" \
  -DGridKit_ENABLE_SUNDIALS=ON \
  -DGridKit_ENABLE_ENZYME=ON

cmake --build . -j$(sysctl -n hw.logicalcpu)
cmake --install .

GridKit uses CMake + make.
cmake --build runs make under the hood with parallel jobs.
cmake --install copies libraries and headers to the install/ prefix.
The build type must be RelWithDebInfo or Release when Enzyme is enabled
— Enzyme has a known bug with -O0 (Debug mode).

Step 5: Test Results
✓  65/66 tests passed in 19.04 seconds

One test failed:
✗  Test #44: EnzymePowerElectronicsCheck — floating point epsilon mismatch
The autodiff Jacobian computed 2.06027e-14 where the reference expects 0. This is effectively machine epsilon on ARM — the values are numerically identical. This is a known tolerance issue on Apple Silicon and does not affect GridKit functionality.

VARIFICATION:
cd ~/Documents/ORNL/src/ornl_gridkit/build
ctest --output-on-failure
With SUNDIALS and Enzyme both enabled, you should see nearly all tests pass.

Issues: 
We use same compilor because Sundials, Enzyme and GridKit are closely related. 
If one component is build on the apple/clang 17 while the other is build of the llvm/ clang 18:
    - linking errors and incompible libaraies can occur. 
    
Compiler Selection:
- This project uses LLVM/Clang 18 exclusively (not Apple Clang, not GCC)
- Apple's built-in clang is a modified fork that lags behind upstream LLVM
- GCC is not used because Enzyme AD is an LLVM plugin and requires Clang

To set the active clang:
  sudo port select --set clang mp-clang-18

All three components (SUNDIALS, Enzyme, GridKit) must use the SAME compiler.
Mixing compilers causes ABI mismatches, linking errors, and incompatible libraries.

Verify which clang is active:
  clang --version

Always `rm -rf *` the build directory before reconfiguring after any failure.
